The truth is that tawhid (the oneness of Allah) is a complete system, and shirk is a contradictory system. Their combination is simply impossible. Therefore, in the Islamic system of life all the affairs of life are established upon this principle, and in that system there is no shirk with the Being of Allah. Life runs in this same pattern. This decisive separation is necessary from the Islamic viewpoint both for the caller (da'i) and for those to whom the call is being given.

Sometimes it happens that this pure Islamic conception of life and the jahili (ignorant) conception of life become mixed together, especially in those societies which had earlier accepted the pure Islamic conception but, with the passage of time, deviation arose within them. When pure faith-based call is presented to such societies, and the Islamic system is presented to them in a simple and straightforward way without any adulteration, these people show great harshness towards this call. Compared to them, the attitude of those people to whom the Islamic call has never reached is more reasonable. This is because societies which had accepted Islam and later deviated are afflicted with the misunderstanding that they too are upon guidance, whereas in their beliefs and practices the corrupt has been mixed with the sound. Sometimes those callers who work among such societies are also deceived, who, while keeping the good aspect of such societies intact, wish to change their bad aspects, and they themselves are deceived by the bad aspects of such societies; and this deception is extremely dangerous.

The real matter is that Islam is Islam and jahiliyyah is jahiliyyah. There is a great difference between them. The proper method is that people should come completely out of jahiliyyah and, having fully left every colour of jahiliyyah, migrate to Islam.

In this process, the first step is that the caller, with complete awareness, comes out of jahiliyyah and towards Islam, in respect of his conceptions and ideas, and in respect of his deeds and method; and this separation should be such that there is no reconciliation between the two, no cultural reconciliation. When someone has fully come out of jahiliyyah and entered Islam, then no cooperation remains between the two. Then it does not happen that fragments and patches of another culture are attached to the cloak of Islam, nor does the principle of give-and-take operate. Neither leaning from this side nor leaning from that side takes place, even if jahiliyyah comes in the guise of Islam and speaks in the name of Islam.

The truth is that for any caller, first of all it is necessary that his mind be clear from this angle; this is the fundamental matter. He should have complete awareness that he is a stranger to that society: "They have their religion and I have my religion; they have their way and I have my way," and he cannot walk even one step on the path of such people. Therefore his duty is to walk on his own path, and without any compromise he should remain so firmly fixed on his path that not a single step is moved from its place. In short, the complete declaration of disavowal is necessary, complete separation is necessary, and a clear and decisive word is necessary.

Lakum dinukum wa liya din (109:6) "For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."

Today's callers to truth are in need of this, and it is extremely necessary for them that they declare their complete disavowal against modern jahiliyyah, and announce a clear and decisive separation. Today's callers need this awareness, that they should well understand that in reality they wish to re-establish and revive Islam anew in a completely jahili and disbelieving society, and they face societies which were once true Muslims. A long period has passed over them.

Fa qasat ... fasiqun ("So their hearts became hard, and most of them became defiant transgressors," 57:16). There is no middle course other than this. Neither can there be a matter of give-and-take, nor the notion that the society is Islamic and only a few faults need reform, that a complete garment is fine and only one patch is needed. The proper method is that the call to Islam be given completely in the same manner in which the true caller gave the complete call at the beginning of Islam, when he was changing a jahili society. Complete separation and distinction between Islam and jahiliyyah is necessary. This is my religion: purely in its beliefs and ideologies, in its Shari'ah and law, and its conceptions and thoughts, all of which are derived from Allah. In it there is no trace or admixture of shirk, and in every aspect of human life and every dimension of human conduct.

There is no alternative to this decisive separation, otherwise confusion with jahiliyyah will remain. Other cultures will be grafted onto Islamic culture, and whatever movement arises will be upon weak and feeble foundations. For the Islamic call and movement it is necessary that it be given with courage, in a clear and decisive manner, and this was the method of the first caller. They spoke plainly.

Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun (109:1) "Say: O disbelievers." Allah addressed them with the word that truly applies to them. They were called by a quality that was actually present in them. In reality they did not follow any religion, and in reality they were not believers; they were disbelievers. Therefore there is no point of commonality between you and them.

In this way, from the very beginning of the surah, a sign is given, and at once it is made clear that a Muslim believer and a disbeliever can never be united.

La a'budu ma ta'budun (109:2) "I do not worship what you worship." My worship differs from your worship, and my object of worship differs from your object of worship.

Wa la antum 'abidun ma a'bud (109:3) "Nor are you worshippers of what I worship." This is because your worship differs from my worship, and your object of worship is other than my object of worship.

Wa la ana 'abidun ma 'abadtum (109:4) "Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped." This is an emphasis of the first clause, but it is negation through the negative nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah manfiyyah). The negative nominal sentence negates a matter with great firmness, permanence and continuity.

Wa la antum 'abidun ma a'bud (109:5) "Nor are you worshippers of what I worship." This is an emphasis of the second clause, so that no doubt remains in this matter. Clearly, after such repeated emphases, there is no room left for doubt.

After this, in a single very concise sentence, a separation is made between the two groups in which no unity remains. Such difference arises that after it no connection remains; between the two there is such separation that after it no meeting can be conceived.

Lakum dinukum wa liya din (109:6) "For you is your religion, and for me is my religion." Here I stand firm on my position and you stand firm on your position; between the two there is no bridge on which these parties could meet. Between the two there is complete separation: a clear distinction and a deep divide.

This complete separation was also necessary, so that the essential contradiction between disbelief and Islam becomes clearer in its features, and seeing it, everyone understands that reconciliation between the two, and a policy of give-and-take, is simply not possible. This is because the difference lies in fundamental principles. The original conception and the way of life are different, and the manner of living is also entirely distinct.

The truth is that tawhid (the oneness of Allah) is a complete system, and shirk is a contradictory system. Their combination is simply impossible. Tawhid is a system and conception which directs man, together with the whole universe, towards Allah alone, without partner, and fixes the direction and orientation from which man is to take guidance for his entire life: beliefs as well as law, values and standards of life, manners as well as ethics. In short, man takes the complete philosophy about this life and this universe from that direction, and the direction from which the believer takes all of this is the direction of the Being of Allah the Exalted, with whom none is a partner. Therefore, in the Islamic system of life all the affairs of life are established upon this principle, and in that system there is no shirk with the Being of Allah. Life runs in this same pattern. This decisive separation is necessary from the Islamic viewpoint both for the caller (da'i) and for those to whom the call is being given.

Sometimes it happens that this pure Islamic conception of life and the jahili (ignorant) conception of life become mixed together, especially in those societies which had earlier accepted the pure Islamic conception but, with the passage of time, deviation arose within them. When pure faith-based call is presented to such societies, and the Islamic system is presented to them in a simple and straightforward way without any adulteration, these people show great harshness towards this call. Compared to them, the attitude of those people to whom the Islamic call has never reached is more reasonable. This is because societies which had accepted Islam and later deviated are afflicted with the misunderstanding that they too are upon guidance, whereas in their beliefs and practices the corrupt has been mixed with the sound. Sometimes those callers who work among such societies are also deceived, who, while keeping the good aspect of such societies intact, wish to change their bad aspects, and they themselves are deceived by the bad aspects of such societies; and this deception is extremely dangerous.

The real matter is that Islam is Islam and jahiliyyah is jahiliyyah. There is a great difference between them. The proper method is that people should come completely out of jahiliyyah and, having fully left every colour of jahiliyyah, migrate to Islam.

In this process, the first step is that the caller, with complete awareness, comes out of jahiliyyah and towards Islam, in respect of his conceptions and ideas, and in respect of his deeds and method; and this separation should be such that there is no reconciliation between the two, no cultural reconciliation. When someone has fully come out of jahiliyyah and entered Islam, then no cooperation remains between the two. Then it does not happen that fragments and patches of another culture are attached to the cloak of Islam, nor does the principle of give-and-take operate. Neither leaning from this side nor leaning from that side takes place, even if jahiliyyah comes in the guise of Islam and speaks in the name of Islam.

The truth is that for any caller, first of all it is necessary that his mind be clear from this angle; this is the fundamental matter. He should have complete awareness that he is a stranger to that society: "They have their religion and I have my religion; they have their way and I have my way," and he cannot walk even one step on the path of such people. Therefore his duty is to walk on his own path, and without any compromise he should remain so firmly fixed on his path that not a single step is moved from its place. In short, the complete declaration of disavowal is necessary, complete separation is necessary, and a clear and decisive word is necessary.

Lakum dinukum wa liya din (109:6) "For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."

Today's callers to truth are in need of this, and it is extremely necessary for them that they declare their complete disavowal against modern jahiliyyah, and announce a clear and decisive separation. Today's callers need this awareness, that they should well understand that in reality they wish to re-establish and revive Islam anew in a completely jahili and disbelieving society, and they face societies which were once true Muslims. A long period has passed over them.

Fa qasat ... fasiqun ("So their hearts became hard, and most of them became defiant transgressors," 57:16). There is no middle course other than this. Neither can there be a matter of give-and-take, nor the notion that the society is Islamic and only a few faults need reform, that a complete garment is fine and only one patch is needed. The proper method is that the call to Islam be given completely in the same manner in which the true caller gave the complete call at the beginning of Islam, when he was changing a jahili society. Complete separation and distinction between Islam and jahiliyyah is necessary. This is my religion: purely in its beliefs and ideologies, in its Shari'ah and law, and its conceptions and thoughts, all of which are derived from Allah. In it there is no trace or admixture of shirk, and in every aspect of human life and every dimension of human conduct.

There is no alternative to this decisive separation, otherwise confusion with jahiliyyah will remain. Other cultures will be grafted onto Islamic culture, and whatever movement arises will be upon weak and feeble foundations. For the Islamic call and movement it is necessary that it be given with courage, in a clear and decisive manner, and this was the method of the first caller. They spoke plainly.

Lakum dinukum wa liya din (109:6) "For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."
